title: When Is Termite Season in Central Texas?
description: General termite-season information for Central Texas homeowners. Excel does not list termite treatment or inspection among its current services.
summary: General identification information only. Termite treatment and inspections are not part of Excel Pest's current advertised service list.
quick_answer: In Central Texas, termites can stay active through much of the year. Swarms are often noticed during warm, humid periods in spring, especially after rain, but an inspection is appropriate whenever you see winged insects, mud tubes or damaged wood.
body_html:
Service note: Excel Pest does not currently advertise termite treatment or termite inspections. This article is general information, not an offer of that service. Contact a licensed termite-service provider for assessment.

Central Texas weather gives termites a long runway. Subterranean termites need moisture and can remain active when temperatures are mild, so waiting for a particular month is not a protection strategy. For homes in Buda, Kyle, San Marcos and Dripping Springs, the better question is whether there are conditions that invite them close to the structure.

Why spring brings more calls

Homeowners often see winged reproductive termites, called swarmers, during warm and humid stretches in spring. A swarm does not tell you exactly where a colony is, but it does mean the conditions are right to investigate. Discarded wings around windowsills, doors or light fixtures are another reason to look more closely.

Signs that deserve an inspection

  • Shelter tubes climbing a foundation, pier, wall or plumbing penetration.
  • Wood that sounds hollow or shows unexplained blistering, soft spots or maze-like damage.
  • Recurring winged insects indoors, particularly if they have straight antennae and equal-length wings.
  • Moisture near the foundation, including leaking spigots, poor drainage or A/C condensate that keeps soil wet.

Reduce the conditions termites like

Keep mulch and wood debris from sitting directly against the exterior, correct drainage problems, and avoid allowing irrigation to soak the foundation. These practical steps help, but they do not replace a qualified inspection when there is evidence of activity.

Where to seek help

If you see suspected termite activity, arrange an assessment with a licensed provider that offers termite services. Excel\'s current service directory lists the pests and services it advertises.

faqs.q: Are winged ants the same as termite swarmers?
faqs.a: No. Flying ants usually have elbowed antennae, a pinched waist and uneven wing lengths. Termite swarmers typically have straighter antennae, a broader waist and wings of similar length. A professional can identify a sample if you are unsure.

faqs.q: Can termites be active in winter in Central Texas?
faqs.a: Yes. Activity may be less visible during colder periods, but termites can remain active in protected areas of a structure and soil. Year-round prevention and inspection matter in this climate.
